note: Unselected episodic migraine: olcegepant (IV) proved the class in 2004, oral telcagepant and MK-3207 were dropped for liver signals on repeated dosing, and ubrogepant, rimegepant and atogepant reached approval 2019-21.
label: Migraine (gepants)

engagement.note: Merck validated capsaicin-evoked CGRP vasodilation by laser Doppler in rhesus forearm as a non-invasive readout for antagonists (olcegepant analog).
engagement.quote: In conclusion, this is the first report to describe and validate a noninvasive model in nonhuman primates that allows rapid evaluation of CGRP antagonist activity against endogenous CGRP.
engagement.judgement: Rodent receptors bind gepants >100-fold weaker, so the class's in vivo work ran in primates; the marmoset trigeminal-stimulation model (Doods 2000) preceded this but was terminal and invasive. model_filed=true because FDA's 2019 ubrogepant pharmacology review names capsaicin-induced vasodilation in rhesus as the in vivo functional model.

engagement.note: Telcagepant blocked capsaicin-evoked skin vasodilation in 12 healthy men with EC90 909 nM, beside 994 nM in rhesus (Salvatore 2008).
engagement.quote: The pharmacodynamic model suggested that the EC90 for telcagepant inhibition of capsaicin-induced increases in DBF was 909 nM.
engagement.reason: Human EC90 909 nM vs rhesus 994 nM
engagement.judgement: The 994 nM rhesus EC90 is my juxtaposition from Salvatore 2008 (doi 10.1124/jpet.107.130344); Sinclair cites the rhesus assay as the origin of the human one but does not print the rhesus number, hence comparison_stated=false and medium confidence (abstract plus partial open-access text; no NCT given, phase 1 Leuven study). Moore 2020 (doi 10.1124/jpet.119.261065) later states the comparison in one source for ubrogepant: CIDV EC50 3.2 nM rhesus vs 2.6 nM human. Central engagement is a separate finding: rhesus-validated PET with [11C]MK-4232 (Hostetler 2013, doi 10.1124/jpet.113.206458; NCT01315847, results posted 2014-10-24) showed only low brain receptor occupancy at the efficacious 140 mg telcagepant dose, so the engagement that tracks efficacy is peripheral. Unit written as nM; PubMed renders the journal's small-caps unit as 'nm'.

dose.note: Rhesus CIDV set telcagepant's exposure target: 127 nM plasma for half-block, 994 nM for 90% block.
dose.quote: MK-0974 produced a concentration-dependent inhibition of dermal vasodilation, generated by capsaicin-induced release of endogenous CGRP, with plasma concentrations of 127 and 994 nM required to block 50 and 90% of the blood flow increase, respectively.
dose.judgement: Abstract-level. MK-3207 was later run through the same rhesus assay (Salvatore 2010, doi 10.1124/jpet.109.163816: 0.8 nM / 7 nM for 50 / 90% block).

dose.model: Human CIDV PK/PD in healthy volunteers, translated from rhesus
dose.note: CIDV EC90 target tracked telcagepant's efficacious 300 mg; for MK-3207 it predicted >=20 mg, plateau 40-100 mg, but only 200 mg was clearly significant.
dose.quote: A similar correlation was established based on clinical CIDV and clinical efficacy data of telcagepant at a 300 mg dose, which was shown in phase 3 studies to be clinically efficacious for acute treatment of migraine.
dose.reason: CIDV EC90 tracked efficacious telcagepant dose
dose.judgement: Open-access full text read. Two comparisons sit in this source: telcagepant (human EC90 909 nM; 300 mg gave 720 nM at 1 h and was the efficacious phase 3 dose; NCT00432237 results posted 2010-12-06, NCT00442936 2014-08-04) is the anchor and is within 2x of the rhesus 994 nM; MK-3207 is weaker - the model predicted efficacy from 20 mg with a plateau at 40-100 mg, while the phase 2 trial (Hewitt 2011, doi 10.1177/0333102411398399; NCT00712725, results posted 2010-11-22, the registry_date used) added 200 mg for insufficient efficacy at 20-100 mg and only 200 mg was significant pairwise, i.e. a 2-5x gap. The authors call it a 'reasonable correlation' and note overlapping CIs across 10-200 mg, so I kept `same` rather than `contra`; magnitude recorded for the telcagepant anchor.

efficacy.note: Olcegepant 1-30 ug/kg IV blocked trigeminally released CGRP's effect on marmoset facial blood flow; nonhuman primate needed because rodent receptors bind gepants >100x weaker.
efficacy.quote: In an in vivo model, BIBN4096BS in doses between 1 and 30 micrograms kg-1 (i.v.) inhibited the effects of CGRP, released by stimulation of the trigeminal ganglion, on facial blood flow in marmoset monkeys.
efficacy.judgement: Olcegepant was never filed, so model_filed is unknown for the marmoset; rimegepant's discovery paper (Luo 2012, doi 10.1021/jm3013147) used the same primate facial-blood-flow model and its FDA review was not checked within budget.

efficacy.note: First-in-class proof of concept: olcegepant 2.5 mg IV gave 66% response at 2 h versus 27% on placebo in 126 migraine patients.
efficacy.quote: The 2.5-mg dose was selected, with a response rate of 66 percent, as compared with 27 percent for placebo (P=0.001).
efficacy.judgement: Abstract only (NEJM paywalled); whether the paper itself sets the marmoset data beside the trial was not verified, hence comparison_stated=false. Trial ran 2002-03, before registration, so no NCT. Status stays `same` through 2022: rhesus CIDV replaced the marmoset as the class's 'animal efficacy model' (the phrase FDA's 2019 ubrogepant pharmacology review uses) and every gepant active in it - telcagepant, MK-3207, ubrogepant - was efficacious in patients; no gepant has failed on efficacy, so `neg` is unavailable and nothing contradicts. The human CGRP-infusion headache model (Petersen 2005, doi 10.1016/j.clpt.2004.10.001; olcegepant abolished CGRP-induced headache in 6/6 volunteers) is a second, human, efficacy model but was published after the trial and is not the model the class relied on.

safety.model: Rat and monkey toxicology (telcagepant; never published or filed)
safety.note: Daily telcagepant raised ALT >=3xULN in 13 patients (2.5%), halting the prevention trial; no published animal-toxicology comparison exists.
safety.quote: Thirteen patients, all in the telcagepant groups, had an alanine aminotransferase (ALT) elevation ≥ 3 × the upper limit of normal and 7 of these also had an aspartate aminotransferase elevation ≥ 3 × the upper limit of normal.
safety.judgement: Trial NCT00797667 stopped 2009, results posted 2014-09-08. By the brief's wording ('or its silence') this is a contra for the animal toxicology - patients got liver injury the rat/monkey studies never flagged - but Merck neither published nor filed telcagepant's toxicology, Ho 2014's full text (HTTP 403) could not be checked for a statement on it, and the FDA ubrogepant review only says two earlier antagonists 'were discontinued because of hepatotoxicity'. No primary source documents the silence, so left `untested` rather than stretched. MK-3207 was likewise dropped for delayed liver-test abnormalities after a positive phase 2 (Hewitt 2011, doi 10.1177/0333102411398399). Abstract-level.

safety.model: In vitro hepatotoxicity assays (bile-acid transporters, mitochondria, oxidative stress) plus DILIsym QST simulation
safety.note: After telcagepant and MK-3207, ubrogepant's filing added HepG2/HepaRG assays and DILIsym simulation, which predicted no ALT elevations.
safety.short: In vitro + QST predict clean liver
safety.quote: The hepatotoxic potential of ubrogepant was assessed in bile acid transporter inhibition, mitochondria function, and oxidative stress assays; ubrogepant was not predicted to be hepatotoxic.
safety.judgement: FDA pharmacology review of NDA 211765 (Nesti, 2019; Reference ID 4535137), read in full text. The review also records rat ALT rises up to 3.2-fold in the standard toxicology for a drug that proved clinically clean, so the conventional animal battery is a poor discriminator here; the sponsor's in vitro/in silico package was explicitly benchmarked against 'two other CGRP receptor antagonists, for which development was discontinued because of hepatotoxicity'.

safety.model: In vitro hepatotoxicity assays plus DILIsym QST simulation
safety.note: DILIsym predicted no liver injury for rimegepant, zavegepant, atogepant, ubrogepant; trials and three FDA labels without hepatic warnings agreed; telcagepant flagged only retrospectively.
safety.short: QST clean-liver calls held in trials
safety.quote: Subsequent clinical trials have validated these predictions for each of the 4 compounds, and all 3 of the compounds submitted to FDA to date (rimegepant, ubrogepant, and atogepant) have since been approved by the FDA with no warning for hepatotoxicity.
safety.reason: QST clean-liver predictions held in trials
safety.judgement: Open-access full text read (Toxicol Sci 188:108-116). Not `neg`: the model's telcagepant flag was generated in 2022, thirteen years after the drug failed, so telcagepant did not 'go on to fail' and a retrospective flag does not prove discrimination; the prospective half (four next-generation gepants predicted clean, confirmed in trials and labels) is a genuine `same`. Authors are DILIsym Services (model vendor) and Biohaven (rimegepant/zavegepant sponsor), hence medium confidence. registry_date is the ubrogepant 52-week safety extension NCT02873221 (results posted 2019-08-28); the dedicated healthy-volunteer high-frequency hepatic-safety study (Goadsby 2019, Cephalalgia) was not located on the registry within budget.
